mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct SI base unit for measuring time?
mcqs.explanation: The International System of Units (SI) defines the second as the base unit of time. It is defined by the duration of 9,192,631,770 periods of the radiation corresponding to the transition between two hyperfine levels of the ground state of the cesium‑133 atom. Minute, hour and day are derived units, not base units, and therefore are not the SI unit of time.

mcqs.question: A student wants to determine the time taken for a ball to fall from a height of 2 m using a handheld stopwatch. Which procedure will give the most accurate measurement of the time interval?

options.A: Start the stopwatch at the instant the ball is released and stop it the moment it hits the ground.
options.B: Start the stopwatch when the ball reaches its highest point and stop it at its lowest point.
options.C: Record the time for many successive drops and use the average of those readings.
options.D: Use a digital timer that displays only whole‑second values.

mcqs.answer: Record the time for many successive drops and use the average of those readings.
mcqs.explanation: Repeated measurements reduce random human reaction‑time errors. By timing several drops and averaging the results, the effect of any single inaccurate start or stop is minimized, giving a more reliable estimate of the true time interval. Options A and B rely on a single reaction, and D lacks the resolution needed for short intervals.

mcqs.question: Three clocks are compared: (i) a mechanical pendulum clock, (ii) a quartz crystal oscillator, and (iii) a cesium atomic clock. Which statement correctly compares their precision?

options.A: The pendulum clock is the most precise of the three.
options.B: The quartz crystal oscillator is more precise than the atomic clock.
options.C: The cesium atomic clock provides the highest precision.
options.D: All three clocks have essentially the same precision.

mcqs.answer: The cesium atomic clock provides the highest precision.
mcqs.explanation: Atomic clocks, such as those based on the hyperfine transition of cesium‑133, achieve precisions better than 10⁻¹⁵ s, far surpassing quartz oscillators (≈10⁻⁹ s) and mechanical pendulums (≈10⁻⁶ s). Hence, the atomic clock is the most precise. Options A, B, and D incorrectly rank the devices.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise periodic phenomena used for timekeeping
mcqs.question: Which periodic phenomenon forms the basis of the definition of the second in the International System of Units (SI) as used in modern atomic clocks?

options.A: Vibration of a quartz crystal at 32,768 Hz
options.C: The hyperfine transition frequency of the ground state of cesium‑133 atoms
options.D: The oscillation of a pendulum of length 1 m

mcqs.answer: The hyperfine transition frequency of the ground state of cesium‑133 atoms
mcqs.explanation: Since 1967, the SI second has been defined as the duration of 9,192,631,770 cycles of the radiation corresponding to the hyperfine transition between the two ground‑state levels of the cesium‑133 atom. This periodic phenomenon provides the most stable and reproducible reference for timekeeping. Options A, B, and D describe other time‑keeping methods but are not the SI definition.
